transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

Well, I'm here because I just... I keep snapping at people lately. Like, we had this safety meeting at work recently—I'm an inspector—and I just started yelling before I could even stop myself. It's gotten to the point where the younger inspectors act like they're scared to even ask me anything. I just need to figure out why I'm acting like this and get a handle on it.
Have you been feeling irritable most of the time lately?

Yeah, like I was just saying, that's exactly it. It feels like it's all the time now. That's why I brought up how I've been snapping at people and losing my temper at that safety meeting. I just... I get set off and the yelling starts before I can even catch myself to rein it in. So, yes, definitely.
Have you always been this irritable, or is this a change from how you used to be?

No, I used to be pretty even-keeled. This is definitely a change. It all started after... well, there was a machinery accident at work after they changed our schedule to overnights. That was about two years and four months ago, and this has been going on ever since then.
Have you been feeling sad or depressed lately?

No, not really. I wouldn't say I feel sad or... depressed. It's not like I'm crying or feeling down in the dumps or anything like that. It's really just the temper and snapping at people like I mentioned.
Would you say that your irritability and snapping at people is part of a broader pattern of behavior that you've noticed in yourself over time?

No, I don't think so. I mean, it's not like this is just how I am or some pattern I've always had. Like I said, it really just started after the accident at work. Before that, I was fine. I didn't have these issues with my temper at all. So, no, I wouldn't call it a broader pattern.
Has your irritability been constant since it started after the accident, or have you had periods where it wasn't as bad?

I don't really know for sure. I haven't kept track of it like that. It feels like it's just been pretty constant... like I'm always just ready to snap. If there were times when it wasn't as bad, I guess I just haven't noticed them.
Do you find that your mood can shift rapidly, like from irritability to another emotional state and back again?

No, I wouldn't say my mood shifts rapidly like that. It's not like I'm irritable one minute and then suddenly fine or feeling something else the next. It's more of just a steady feeling of being on edge and easily frustrated. I don't really bounce around between different emotions.
Has your irritability been getting worse over the past two years since it started?

I'm not really sure if it's getting worse, to be honest. It just... it feels about the same. Like I said, it's just been pretty constant this whole time. I haven't really noticed it getting more intense or anything, it's just always there, making me feel on edge.
Is there something specific that usually triggers your irritability and snapping at people?

I'm not really sure if it's one specific thing, honestly. I just... I keep snapping at people over nothing. Like, we had a safety meeting recently, and I just started yelling before I could even stop myself. It just came out. And now the younger inspectors at work act scared to even come up and ask me anything.
Do you think your irritability is something that you've learned to live with as part of who you are now?

I don't know if I'd say that. I haven't really... thought about it like it's just who I am now. I definitely don't want it to be. It's just something that's happening, and I'm stuck dealing with it. I wouldn't say I've learned to live with it, really, it's just... there.
Do you think you've always had some tendency towards being irritable, even before the accident at work?

No, I really don't think so. Before the accident, I was pretty... well, just even-tempered, I guess. I mean, everyone gets annoyed on the job sometimes, but I never used to fly off the handle or yell at people. This whole thing where I just snap without warning... that definitely only started after the accident.
Would you describe yourself as someone who has always had a bit of a temper, even as a child or teenager?

No, I wouldn't say that. I... I was a pretty normal kid, honestly. I didn't get into fights or throw fits as a teenager. I mostly just got along with people. I never really had a temper at all until... well, until the accident happened.
Do you think you would still be considered an irritable person even when you're not stressed or under pressure?

No, I don't think so. I mean, honestly, it's hard to tell these days because it feels like I'm always stressed or on edge about something. But... if I really think about a time when I'm just sitting at home, completely relaxed, no pressure... I don't feel irritable then. It's really just when things start piling up or people are in my face. So, no, I wouldn't say I'm just an irritable person all the time.
Do you think you've become more prone to irritability in all areas of your life, not just at work?

Yes, it's definitely spilling over. It's not just at work, though that's a big part of it. I'm actually here because I just keep snapping at people everywhere. Like... the other day at work, we had this safety meeting, and I just started yelling at someone. I didn't even realize I was doing it until I was already shouting. I couldn't stop myself. And now... well, the younger inspectors at the plant, they act like they're scared to even ask me a question. But it's happening at home, too, and at the grocery store. I just have this incredibly short fuse now.
Do you think you would describe yourself as an irritable person even when you're not under any specific stress or pressure?

I think I just mentioned this a moment ago, but no, I wouldn't. If I'm not under any stress at all and I'm just relaxing at home, I'm not irritable. I feel fine then. It really only happens when the pressure is on or things start getting to me.
Do you think you'll always be an irritable person from now on?

I really hope not. I mean, I don't know for sure, but... I don't want to be like this forever. It's exhausting living with this short of a fuse. I'm hoping that by being here, maybe I can figure out how to get back to how I used to be, or at least get a handle on it. But right now... I just don't know.
Do you think your irritability is something that is a part of your personality now?

I don't know... I haven't really thought about it like that. I certainly don't want it to be who I am. Like I said, I didn't used to be this way. I just know I'm snapping at people all the time right now, but whether it's actually become my personality... I'm really not sure. I guess it kind of feels like it lately, but I don't know for certain.
Do you think you'll always have this irritable nature?

I feel like we're kind of going in circles with this, but... I really don't know. Like I just said, I hope not. I don't want to be stuck with this kind of nature for the rest of my life. I want to get better. But I just can't say for sure what's going to happen down the road.
Do you think your irritability is a fundamental part of who you are as a person?

Doctor, I really feel like you're asking me the exact same thing again. No, I don't think it's a fundamental part of who I am. I lived well over fifty years not being this way. It's just... what I'm dealing with right now. I really don't have a different answer to give you on this.
Do you think you will always have this irritable nature?

I'm sorry, but you literally just asked me that exact same question a minute ago. I don't know what else to tell you. Like I said before, I really hope I won't always be this way, because I want to get better. But I can't predict the future. I just don't have a different answer to give you.
